sections.title: Physical health
sections.content:
Advanced vocabulary for discussing health conditions and treatment:
• chronic — lasting for a long time. She suffers from chronic back pain.
• contagious — spread from person to person. The flu is highly contagious in winter.
• diagnosis — identification of an illness. The doctor's diagnosis was surprisingly accurate.
• remedy — a treatment for illness. Hot tea with honey is a popular home remedy for colds.
• symptom — a sign of illness. Fatigue is a common symptom of many conditions.

sections.title: Mental health
sections.content:
Discussing mental well-being requires sensitive and precise vocabulary:
• anxiety — persistent worry and unease. Anxiety about exams is very common among students.
• therapy — treatment through conversation or activity. Cognitive behavioural therapy has proven very effective.
• mindfulness — awareness of the present moment. Practising mindfulness can reduce daily stress levels.
• well-being — the state of being comfortable and healthy. Companies are investing more in employee well-being.
• stigma — negative attitudes towards something. There is still stigma around mental health in many cultures.

sections.title: Lifestyle and prevention
sections.content:
Words related to staying healthy:
• sedentary — involving much sitting and little exercise. A sedentary lifestyle increases health risks.
• balanced diet — eating a healthy variety of foods. A balanced diet includes fruit, vegetables, and protein.
• immune system — the body's defence against disease. Regular exercise strengthens your immune system.
• holistic — treating the whole person, not just symptoms. She prefers a holistic approach to health.

exercises.question: A condition that lasts for a very long time is described as:
exercises.hint: The opposite of short-term or acute.
exercises.explanation: Chronic means persisting for a long time or constantly recurring.

exercises.question: A lifestyle with too much sitting and little physical activity is:
exercises.hint: Office workers often have this type of lifestyle.
exercises.explanation: Sedentary means tending to spend much time seated; inactive.

exercises.question: Negative attitudes or shame associated with a condition is called:
exercises.hint: It prevents people from seeking help.
exercises.explanation: Stigma is a mark of disgrace associated with a particular condition or quality.

exercises.question: An approach that considers the whole person, not just symptoms, is:
exercises.explanation: Holistic means relating to the treatment of the whole person, including mental and social factors.

exercises.question: The body's natural defence system against disease is the:
exercises.explanation: The immune system is a network of cells and organs that defends the body against infection.

exercises.question: Being focused on the present moment without judgement is:
exercises.explanation: Mindfulness is a mental state achieved by focusing on the present moment calmly.

exercises.question: A disease that spreads from one person to another is:
exercises.hint: You can catch it from someone else.
exercises.explanation: Contagious means spread from one person to another by direct or indirect contact.

exercises.question: The identification of an illness by a doctor is called a:
exercises.hint: The doctor tells you what's wrong.
exercises.explanation: A diagnosis is the identification of the nature of an illness by examination of the symptoms.
